directoryStems.mcq-672a2233d40478f8ffec6636: בן 80, מועמד לניתוח להחלפת פרק ירך, אובחן כסובל משבריריות (FRAILITY) על פי הקריטריונים של FRIED. ברקע - סוכרת, אי ספיקת כליות מתקדמת ומחלת לב איסכמית. מה ההשפעה של השבריריות (FRAILITY) על בעיותיו הרפואיות?
directoryStems.mcq-29b5d2cb0031081c25ada235: כל הגורמים הבאים נכללים בקריטריונים לשבריריות (FRAILTY) לפי FRIED פרט ל-
directoryStems.mcq-6df632c6cbeac8fa6876ac5f: בת 87 מתלוננת שסובלת בשנה האחרונה מחולשה ותשישות כללית. היא ירדה במשקל מירידה במשקל (מ-65 ק"ג ל- 59 ק"ג). מדווחת שירדה בפעילות (מסתגרת בבית, הפסיקה לצאת לקניות, הפסיקה לנהוג ברכב). היא החלה ללכת עם מקל משום שהליכתה לא יציבה, ואף מעדה ונפלה פעם אחת ברחוב ומאז חוששת לצאת מהבית. מדווחת גם על ירידה בזיכרון לטווח הקצר בחודשים האחרונים. מה מהממצאים של החולה מתאימים למאפיינים של FRAILTY לפי FRIED?
directoryStems.mcq-30c82a2cc97c7930197d674a: In the Fried frailty phenotype, meeting at least three of five criteria identifies frailty. What underlying process does this model propose?
directoryStems.mcq-b908f69d4209b7df1626ff41: What does the term inflammaging describe in Hazzard?
directoryStems.mcq-d6e4989704d2ecdd8b9bcf09: A 78-year-old woman attends routine follow-up. She reports unintentional loss of 4 kg in six months, increased exhaustion, and difficulty walking to her mailbox without resting. She has hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and osteoarthritis. Examination finds reduced grip strength and slow gait. Her medication regimen is stable, and she has no acute medical illness. Which interpretation follows Hazzard's description of the Fried frailty phenotype?
directoryStems.mcq-b2952aa21770b352a5cbc44b: A 75-year-old woman with COPD, osteoporosis, and depression has not returned to her previous function two months after hospitalization for pneumonia. She remains weak, has reduced appetite, and now uses a walker although she previously walked independently. Which physiologic concept in Hazzard's frailty model explains vulnerability to stress and impaired recovery?
directoryStems.mcq-b02034474131921b67085132: An 85-year-old woman with heart failure, diabetes, and arthritis is evaluated after a fall. Her family reports progressive unsteadiness, weight loss, and increased confusion. Examination shows slowness and weak grip. Which feature fits the physical frailty phenotype described by Hazzard?
directoryStems.mcq-0d9c67b9956bfdeaad3acc11: A 72-year-old man has progressive fatigue and functional decline despite well-controlled hypertension, diabetes, and coronary disease. He has become less active, lost weight, and developed sarcopenia and slow gait. Which biological association does Hazzard describe in frailty?
directoryStems.mcq-cd1e5b9e55753699940d9d75: A 68-year-old woman with heart failure, COPD, and osteoarthritis is referred because she appears frail. Her physician requests help with prognosis and treatment planning. Which principle from Hazzard should guide assessment?
directoryStems.mcq-74e2cad216a2756c12498a40: An 80-year-old man with several comorbidities has a prolonged recovery, complications, and a need for rehabilitation after hospitalization for pneumonia. His family asks why recovery remains difficult after the pneumonia has resolved. Which description captures the frailty concept in Hazzard?
directoryStems.mcq-1c1d22553b1e9359cd9cf5c0: A 77-year-old woman has slowed over eighteen months. She has stable diabetes, hypertension, and mild heart failure, reports reduced energy, has unintentionally lost 4 kg, and now uses a cane for stability. Medications are unchanged and recent laboratory results are normal. Which conceptualization from Hazzard is relevant when assessing possible frailty?
directoryStems.mcq-80f80447923ccdae3ce03cfa: An 81-year-old woman with unintentional weight loss, weak grip, and slow walking is being evaluated for frailty. How does Hazzard’s phenotypic model explain frailty?
directoryStems.mcq-1de979eb6f87a866165b9192: An 86-year-old man with coronary artery disease is being considered for an intervention. Cardiac and renal measures are known, but daily function and physiologic reserve have not been assessed. What does frailty assessment add to the discussion?
directoryStems.mcq-bc24e7f8e5a730eac8743b21: An 86-year-old woman has had four falls in three months, each while getting up to use the toilet at night. She has poor appetite, temporal wasting, weight 48 kg, BMI 18, grip strength 12 kg, gait speed 0.6 m/s, and albumin 3.0 g/dL. directoryStems.mcq-709d9ab5d0c401eb1452d6ac: בת 86, תשושה בתפקודה וסובלת מירידה קוגניטיבית קלה. מתגוררת בביתה עם עזרה של "חוק סיעוד". הגיעה למרפאה נפרולוגית למעקב עקב אי ספיקה כלייתית מתקדמת עם CCT-15 מ"ל/דקה. מה הקשר האפשרי בין שבריריות (FRAILTY) לאי ספיקה כלייתית?

directoryStems.mcq-e1593b4c91f0875d66348128: בת 84 מתגוררת בקהילה, עם ירידה במהירות ההליכה, חולשת אחיזה, ירידה בפעילות גופנית ועייפות מתמשכת. ללא על ירידה במשקל בשנה האחרונה. מה הקביעה הנכונה ביותר לגבי אבחנת Frailty לפי ההגדרה של Fried?

highlightAliases.old: Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS): 7-category clinician-judgment scale derived from FI work; similar predictive power to FI for institutionalization/death (p623)
highlightAliases.new: Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS): the original seven-category version used clinical judgment and predicted institutionalization and death similarly to the FI (p623). The current CFS has nine levels.

highlightAliases.old: Table 42-3 (p621) catalogs further named frailty instruments beyond FPP/FI/CFS/EFS — Gill Frailty Measure, Brief Frailty Instrument, Vulnerable Elders Survey (VES-13), FRAIL Scale (p621–622) Table 42-3 also spells out the CFS's 7 categories (p621): 1 = very fit; 2 = well (no active disease); 3 = well, with treated comorbid disease; 4 = apparently vulnerable (not frankly dependent, "slowed up"); 5 = mildly frail (IADL help only); 6 = moderately frail (help with IADLs + ADLs); 7 = severely frail (ADL-dependent) or terminally ill VES-13: frail if score ≥3 (range 0–10); FRAIL Scale (fatigue, resistance, ambulation, illness count >5, weight loss >5%): 0 = no frailty, 1–2 = intermediate, ≥3 = frailty (p622)
highlightAliases.new: Table 42-3 (p621) catalogs further named frailty instruments beyond FPP/FI/CFS/EFS — Gill Frailty Measure, Brief Frailty Instrument, Vulnerable Elders Survey (VES-13), FRAIL Scale (p621–622) Table 42-3 also spells out the original CFS’s seven categories (p621): 1 = very fit; 2 = well (no active disease); 3 = well, with treated comorbid disease; 4 = apparently vulnerable (not frankly dependent, "slowed up"); 5 = mildly frail (IADL help only); 6 = moderately frail (help with IADLs + ADLs); 7 = severely frail (ADL-dependent) or terminally ill. The current nine-point CFS scores terminal illness as 9. VES-13: frail if score ≥3 (range 0–10); FRAIL Scale (fatigue, resistance, ambulation, ≥5 of 11 specified illnesses, weight loss ≥5% over the preceding year): 0 = no frailty, 1–2 = intermediate, ≥3 = frailty (p622; validated FRAIL questionnaire, Morley et al., PMCID PMC4515112).
